newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe to resign whoever wins poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe to resign whoever wins poll.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he would resign from the premiership whoever wins next Sunday's parliamentary election runoff after the opposition left outpolled his centre-right coalition in the first round.
Juppe told a meeting of coalition leaders: "We need a new team led by a new prime minister."
Officials said Juppe secretly called on President Jacques Chirac on Monday afternoon before meeting leaders of the centre-right alliance to announce his decision.

The Gaullist premier has borne the brunt of blame for austerity, high taxes and record unemployment in the two years since Chirac took office and was widely held responsible for the conservatives' poor showing in Sunday's first round.

The combined left polled four points more than the centre-right in the first round, and polling institutes projected that the opposition would win a slim majority if the voting pattern was repeated in next Sunday's runoff.
Juppe, 51, is Chirac's longest-serving political associate and aides told reporters only last week that the president hoped to reappoint him if the centre-right won the election.
His decision to sacrifice himself enables Chirac to promise voters a fresh start if they re-elect the coalition rather than forcing him to "cohabit" with a hostile, Socialist-led government.
Juppe said in a statement that the opposition Socialist-Communist alliance was in no position to bring France the change it needs.
"A return to socialism would be the opposite of change. Today the President of the Republic embodies renewal and it is under his leadership that France will renew itself," Juppe said.
"I trust the President of the Republic to choose the men and women who will be able to lead the French people in this new stage.

"As for myself, as leader of our majority and with you, I will lead this fight to the end, until success which is within our reach, after which I will consider my task has been accomplished," he added.
